items.followUp: Compare a true solution and a colloid in four ways.

rubric.description: Suspension particles are larger than colloidal particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly comparing the particle sizes of both mixtures.

rubric.description: Suspension particles can be seen with the naked eye, whereas colloidal particles cannot.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the visibility of particles in both mixtures.

rubric.why: Shows the difference in stability on standing.
rubric.description: Suspension particles settle on standing; colloidal particles remain dispersed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct difference in settling behaviour.

rubric.why: Shows how the mixtures behave during filtration.
rubric.description: Suspension particles can be separated by ordinary filtration; colloidal particles cannot.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct filtration comparison.

rubric.why: Identifies the nature of the mixtures.
rubric.description: Both suspensions and colloids are heterogeneous mixtures, although a colloid may appear uniform.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the mixture nature correctly.

modelAnswer: Suspension particles are larger than colloidal particles.
Suspension particles can be seen with the naked eye; colloidal particles cannot.
Suspension particles settle on standing; colloidal particles remain dispersed.
Suspension particles can be separated by ordinary filtration; colloidal particles cannot.
Both suspensions and colloids are heterogeneous mixtures, though a colloid may appear uniform.

rubric.why: Distinguishes inorganic chemistry from organic chemistry.
rubric.description: Inorganic chemistry is the study of all elements and their compounds except organic compounds.

modelAnswer: Organic chemistry is the study of hydrocarbons and their derivatives.
Inorganic chemistry is the study of all elements and their compounds except organic compounds.

items.followUp: Why does atomic size generally increase down a group?

rubric.why: Checks the increasing nuclear charge across a period.
rubric.description: The number of protons and hence the nuclear charge increases from left to right.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that nuclear charge increases across a period.

rubric.why: Explains how increasing nuclear charge affects the electrons.
rubric.description: Added electrons enter the same shell, while the stronger nuclear attraction pulls them closer to the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking stronger attraction within the same shell to a smaller atomic size.

modelAnswer: From left to right across a period, the number of protons increases, so the nuclear charge increases.
The added electrons enter the same shell; the stronger attraction pulls them closer to the nucleus, decreasing atomic size.
